classification.difficultyReason: Six diagrams, each judged by shared vertex, shared arm and non-overlap. Overlapping angles, a vertically opposite pair and different-vertex pairs are the traps. No reflex case, so slightly lighter than p20-q2, but the demand is essentially the same.

content.prompt: Decide whether the marked angles in each diagram are adjacent.

answer.worked: $\angle UTV$ and $\angle VTW$ share vertex $T$ and arm $TV$, and do not overlap.
$\angle ABC$ and $\angle BCD$ have different vertices, $B$ and $C$.
$\angle LMK$ and $\angle JMN$ share vertex $M$ but have no common arm.
$\angle QYR$ lies inside $\angle PYR$, so they overlap.
$\angle IGH$ and $\angle HGF$ share vertex $G$ and arm $GH$, and do not overlap.
$\angle EZR$ and $\angle RZX$ share vertex $Z$ and arm $ZR$, and do not overlap. Arm $ZS$ lies inside $\angle EZR$ and does not change this.
